narrative_purpose: Makes Fick's law visual: gas crosses a living membrane faster with more surface, a thinner wall, and a steeper difference between the two sides.
subject: A flat schematic cross-section of a thin respiratory membrane shown as a single narrow vertical band down the centre. On the left side, many small glowing dots crowded densely together (high concentration); on the right side, only a few scattered dots (low concentration). Several arrows cross the thin band from the crowded left to the sparse right. The band is drawn deliberately thin, and is wide top-to-bottom to suggest large surface area.
scene: Empty dark space background, only the membrane band, the dot fields, and the crossing arrows.
camera: Flat head-on schematic view, no perspective, no 3D.
light: Flat even lighting; the dots and arrows glow on their own.
palette: Near-black background, dense cyan dots on the left, sparse teal dots on the right, thin pale membrane band, glowing cyan crossing arrows.
style: Clean elegant infographic of thin glowing shapes, like a vector schematic.
detail_level: Crisp clean dots and arrows, an obviously thin central band, generous space; nothing cluttered.
composition: Central thin vertical band, crowded dot field left, sparse dot field right, a few clear arrows crossing left to right.
consistency_notes: Thin glowing cyan/teal shapes on a near-black background; the shared visual language for every schematic diagram in this chapter.
negative_prompt: no text, no letters, no numbers, no busy clutter, no photorealism, no 3D bevels, no drop shadows
